title: What is Carnage Club?
summary: A mobile turn-based RPG about tactical duels, finding your own fighting style, and discovering a dark world at your own pace.
text: The core idea # Carnage Club combines one-on-one duels, character development, and exploration of a fallen hunters’ order. At its heart is an exchange of decisions: you observe the opponent while it gains experience from your actions. The world remembers your habits. Familiar tactics can remain useful, but repetition makes you more predictable. Your build, resource management, and attention to the previous round work together. The game loop # Explore. Move across the map, find encounters, and discover available routes. Prepare. Combine equipment, attributes, abilities, and perks. Decide. Choose attack and defense directions and keep track of your resources. Reflect. The battle log explains the outcome and helps you reconsider the next turn. Three pillars # Tactical duels : the choices of both participants shape the result. Your own build : different tools support different ways of playing. Atmosphere and discovery : encounters, items, and dialogue gradually reveal the world. About this guide # This is a public introduction to a game in development. It explains the main mechanics while leaving the story’s discoveries in the game. Screens show the current version; details may change during development.

title: How a duel works
summary: Combat unfolds in rounds: both participants attack, defend, and see the consequences of their choices.
text: Decisions before action # Each round, you choose attack and defense directions. You also select a defense type and, when appropriate, an active ability. The opponent makes its own choices; resolution brings these decisions together. The turn-based format gives you time to think. Consider the hunter’s condition, the options provided by equipment, and the behavior you have already observed. What shapes the outcome # An attack direction meets the corresponding defense. An uncovered zone, a block, and a parry produce different consequences for health, defensive guard, and stamina. Abilities, perks, and status effects can add to the exchange. Consider the whole round: landing your own attack does not explain what happened in return. What carries into the next round # Changed resources and active effects influence the next decision. The battle log explains the actions, while the adaptive opponent draws on its accumulated experience. Continue with directions , Block and Parry , and combat resources .

title: Attack & defense directions
summary: Four zones turn attacking and defending into specific choices.
text: Four zones # A duel uses four zones: Head, Torso, Belly, and Legs. Your chosen directions determine where an attack is aimed and which zones a defense covers. Your build defines the options # The number of available directions depends on combat capabilities and equipment. Attack, Block, and Parry have their own coverage. Covering several zones with one type of defense does not imply identical coverage with another. This is one reason a new weapon can change the feel of a duel beyond the damage it deals. Observation matters # The previous round gives you information about the opponent’s choices. At the same time, it gains experience from yours. Directions connect that mutual observation to the decision in front of you. Related: defense types and weapon styles .

title: Block & Parry
summary: Two defense types with different resources, coverage, and opportunities to respond.
text: Block: withstand pressure # Blocking is tied to Guard, the resource behind your defensive stance. It lets you meet attacks in covered zones, but sustained pressure wears that protection down. When Guard breaks, the consequences of an attack can reach Health. Consider blocking alongside the hunter’s current condition. Parry: intercept and answer # Parrying uses Stamina. A successful interception allows a counterattack. Parry coverage is defined separately from Block, while equipment and effects influence the opportunities it creates. Why both matter # Defense is part of your build and a decision for the current round. Available directions, resources, perks, and abilities all matter. The same hunter can value these options differently as a fight develops. Continue with Health, Guard, and Stamina and perks .

title: Health, Guard & Stamina
summary: Three resources create different kinds of pressure and shape the options available next round.
text: Health # Health determines whether a participant remains in the duel. Uncovered attacks and certain effects threaten it directly. Other mechanics let a hunter recover Health within the options provided by the build. Guard # Guard supports blocking and the ability to withstand pressure. Wearing down a defensive stance changes the situation even while Health still looks comfortable. A broken Guard makes the exchange more dangerous. Stamina # Stamina powers parrying and many active abilities. Spending it connects a strong action now with the options available in the following round. Read them together # The three bars describe different aspects of the hunter’s condition. High Health does not replace depleted Guard or Stamina. Equipment, progression, and active effects shape how a build handles each resource. Related: status effects and abilities .

title: Status effects & interactions
summary: An action can have lasting consequences that change how the fight develops.
text: Rounds are connected # Status effects keep influencing participants after an individual action has ended. They can deal damage over time, restore a resource, or change combat capabilities. Recognizing an active effect helps you understand the hunter’s current condition. An example: Bleed # Bleeding creates pressure over time. Applying and strengthening it can be part of a combination of abilities, perks, and weapons. Its consequences extend beyond a single direct hit. A build is a set of interactions # Some effects respond to a successful attack, block, or parry. Others help sustain resources. Together they give a hunter a distinctive style: combinations matter alongside individual bonuses. Icons and the battle log help track those consequences. The Codex explains the mechanics.

title: The battle log
summary: Feedback that helps connect a decision with its outcome.
text: See what happened # The log describes actions, attack directions, resource changes, and triggered effects. It complements the battle scene by letting you read an exchange and understand its consequences. Several causes, one outcome # A Health change can involve a direct attack, an ability, a perk, or an active status. Recovery also has a cause. The log helps reveal which parts of your build took part in the round. A basis for the next decision # Observing the exchange teaches you about the opponent’s choices and your own hunter. That is part of a duel with an adaptive opponent: both participants update their understanding through experience. Related: the flow of a duel and adaptive opponents .

title: Character progression
summary: Growing stronger and finding your own way to play go hand in hand.
text: What makes a build # Attributes, equipment, passive perks, and active abilities shape a hunter. Each provides a different kind of option; their combination defines the character’s strengths and weaknesses. Different kinds of growth # Attributes provide the foundation for combat capabilities. Abilities are active tools for a particular moment. Perks support a style through bonuses and reactions. Equipment changes stats and available interactions. The hunter’s experience and yours # Leveling up creates decisions about further development. Your understanding of a duel grows too: why an action worked, where a resource fell short, and how the parts of a build support one another. A new find or option gains its value from its place in the way you currently play.

title: The four attributes
summary: Strength, Fortitude, Mastery, and Focus provide the foundation for character development.
text: The foundation of a hunter # Attributes influence derived combat stats and development options. They work alongside equipment and effects: a single value does not describe the entire build. Four directions of growth # Strength relates to the force of attacks and pressure on an opponent. Fortitude supports a hunter’s resilience and ability to endure. Mastery increases Stamina and supports its recovery. Focus influences the chance of a critical hit. Read them in context # Consider development alongside your weapon, existing perks, and chosen abilities. Attributes set the foundation; the character of a build emerges in the duel. Related: character progression and weapon styles .

title: Active abilities
summary: Tools you choose for a particular situation in a duel.
text: Another decision in a round # An ability complements ordinary attacking and defending. It can increase pressure, apply an effect, help sustain resources, or support defense. Its value depends on the condition of both participants. Cost and readiness # Many abilities use Stamina and have a cooldown. Some require a direction; others do not. Read the conditions of the individual ability: selecting it does not replace meeting its requirements during the exchange. A tool for your style # The game includes abilities connected to bleeding, recovery, and pressure on defenses. Their value comes from how they fit with weapons and perks. Bloodletting and Blood Renewal are among the abilities visible in the screenshots. Related: resources , status effects , and perks .

title: Passive perks
summary: Bonuses and reactions that support a chosen fighting style.
text: A lasting part of the build # Perks complement a hunter without requiring a separate action every round. Some change combat capabilities; others react to events such as a successful attack or parry. Conditions matter # A reactive perk becomes relevant when its triggering event occurs. Its usefulness depends on the hunter’s style, equipment, and decisions. A perk supporting a particular weapon or defense should be considered in that context. Interactions give a build character # Perks can help a hunter withstand pressure, develop bleeding effects, or support parrying. The progression screen shows examples, while the battle log helps reveal their effects in an exchange. Related: progression , weapons , and the battle log .

title: Equipment & discoveries
summary: Items change a hunter’s options and give you reasons to reconsider a familiar build.
text: More than a damage number # Weapons define combat options and support different approaches to attack and defense. Other equipment complements a hunter’s resources, stats, and effects. Choose in the context of a build # Items differ in properties and rarity. Consider what a find changes: strengthening familiar tactics, covering a weakness, or supporting a different combination of abilities and perks. Compare the whole loadout. An individual bonus gains meaning through what the hunter can already do. Objects belong to the world # Named equipment has its own visual identity and a short piece of descriptive writing. It gives the world character while leaving the discoveries around each item to the game. Continue with weapon styles and character progression .

title: Weapon styles
summary: Different weapon combinations support different approaches to a duel.
text: One-handed weapon and shield # This combination supports defensive options and the management of Guard. Exact coverage and effects depend on equipment and character development. Two-handed weapons # Two-handed options emphasize the force of attacks and pressure. The specific item and build interactions define additional capabilities. The inventory screenshot shows Black Maul as one example of this weapon identity. Dual weapons # Dual weapons support their own combinations of attacks, parrying, and reactive effects. Their character emerges alongside perks and Stamina management. A style has several parts # The weapon type sets a direction without describing the entire hunter. Attributes, abilities, and perks can strengthen its advantages or help with its limitations. Related: Block and Parry and perks .

title: Opponents that learn
summary: Experience from previous exchanges influences an opponent’s later decisions.
text: The duel develops # An opponent takes completed actions and their consequences into account. Repeated directions, familiar moves, and interaction outcomes gradually form experience. The present situation matters too: resources and available options change the value of decisions. Observe the opponent in the context of the current fight. Campaign memory # Knowledge about the player’s habits persists between sessions within a campaign. The end of an individual duel does not erase all experience of those interactions. The player learns too # Adaptation creates a mutual process. The enemy gains experience from your actions; the battle scene and log let you see the consequences of its choices. A changed habit or a different build gives the exchange a new direction. Related: the battle log and directions .

title: Exploring the club
summary: The map connects fights, encounters, and preparation into a single journey.
text: The space between duels # The hunter moves across a map of connected places. Available routes determine where you can go at a given moment; exploration reveals encounters and opportunities to continue. A changing rhythm # Combat encounters alternate with dialogue, discoveries, trading, and rest. This creates room for character development and getting to know the world between tense duels. Preparation is a decision # Before another encounter, you can reconsider equipment and the tools available to the hunter. A new item or development option can change the approach you bring back into combat. Route details and the resolutions of local stories remain discoveries for the game. Related: encounters and dialogue and equipment .

title: Encounters & dialogue
summary: The club’s inhabitants and discovered texts gradually give the journey meaning.
text: Meet the world through its inhabitants # Encounters complement combat with other aspects of life in the club. Characters, their words, and surrounding details help establish a place with a past of its own. Dialogue within the journey # A conversation can connect to an encounter, a local story, or further exploration. Narrative scenes and gameplay opportunities work together. The Experiment 403 screenshot illustrates this format: an environment, a portrait, and the character’s text. Leave discoveries to the player # This guide does not reproduce complete conversations, answer sequences, or quest resolutions. Those stories are best discovered through your own journey. Related: the world and atmosphere and exploration .

title: The world & atmosphere
summary: A fallen hunters’ order, gothic spaces, and a power that leaves its mark.
text: A place with a past # Carnage Club grew from a fallen hunters’ order. Its architecture, objects, and encounters retain traces of an earlier life. The hunter comes to know the place through the journey. A gothic visual language # Dark spaces, old ritual motifs, restrained gold, and blood-red accents establish the tone. Illustrated scenes and characters support a dangerous world with rules of its own. The mechanics belong to the world # Weapons, blood abilities, and combat experience connect to the identity of a hunter. Character development becomes part of the journey rather than an isolated set of numbers. The causes of events, hidden connections, and the characters’ later fates remain discoveries for the game. Related: encounters and the project introduction .

title: Hints & the Codex
summary: Reference material helps you understand the rules and make your own decisions.
text: Understand a new tool # Hints and the Codex explain combat resources, actions, and effects. They provide context for what you see in the interface: what a stat means, the role of a defense, and why an effect matters. Explanation and observation # Reference material explains a mechanic; the battle log shows its part in a particular exchange. Together they connect the rules to your own experience of playing. Where to begin # Start with the game overview . For duels, read about combat and resources . Character development has its own pages on builds and equipment . This guide explains the character of the project while leaving narrative discoveries for your own playthrough.
